Every Halloween, I see the same bad candy-and-wine pairings pop up everywhere. The fix is simple: the wine has to hold its own against the sugar. If it doesn’t, the pairing falls flat.

I broke down a few candy pairings that actually make sense, from Reese’s to Sour Patch Kids. Which Halloween candy are you pairing with wine this year?

instagram_reel.hook: Halloween candy and dry wine? That pairing is trouble.
instagram_reel.script:
I need to say this plainly: if your candy is sweeter than your wine, the wine is going to taste thin and sour. That’s why so many Halloween candy pairings miss the mark.

The fix is simple. Match sweetness with sweetness. Match texture too, when you can.

So yes, you can absolutely pair wine with Halloween candy. Reese’s with Oloroso Sherry. Sour Patch Kids with a sweeter Prosecco. NERDS Gummy Clusters with Pink Moscato.

The full list is on the site, and it’s a lot more fun than the usual bad takes.

linkedin.post:
Halloween is a great example of why sweetness matters in food and wine pairing.

When the food is sweeter than the wine, the wine can read as thin, sharp, or flat on the palate. That’s why a lot of the usual Halloween candy and wine suggestions miss the mark.

The solution is straightforward: the wine needs to match the sweetness of the candy, or come in a little sweeter. Texture matters too, especially with chewy, crunchy, or creamy sweets.

That’s what makes pairings like Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups with Oloroso Sherry, Sour Patch Kids with a sweeter Prosecco, and NERDS Gummy Clusters with Pink Moscato work as a starting point.

There’s a real opportunity here for the wine trade: make dessert and holiday pairing guidance more practical, more accurate, and more fun.
